fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Merch Planner, Buyer, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - Assortment auto-suggested from the prior-year same-season sell-through by format; seasonal-PO auto-generated from the approved assortment
Controls: - CTL-39: rebate/co-op terms on seasonal POs validated; operational: VP Merchandising sign-off on the seasonal assortment plan
Pain Points / Risks: - **Import-lead-time risk**: a seasonal SKU sourced via import (40% of COGS) has a 10–12 week lead time, so the PO must place before sell-through signal confirms demand; mitigated by the 3-month-pre-season trigger and the W2399 post-season forecast-accuracy feedback loop

- **Format-mismatch risk**: the compact format can't carry the full seasonal assortment, and over-assortment creates fixture crowding; mitigated by the format-tiered assortment per W299 store-cluster master
System Touchpoints: - Assortment/item master (links to VS-01 / W1 SKU planning, VS-29 / W299 assortment & store-cluster master) — the seasonal SKU set per format
- Seasonal calendar (links to VS-29 / W306 seasonal-calendar master) — the 6-season Philippine retail calendar driving the planning trigger
- Purchase orders (links to VS-03 / W2B import POs, VS-15 P2P) — the seasonal PO placement
Time Estimate: ~4 days Category Manager + ~7.5 days Merch Planner/Buyer × 6 seasons = **~690–840 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Category Manager identifies seasonal opportunities per Philippine calendar: summer (garden, aircon, outdoor), rainy (waterproofing, flood control), ber-months (holiday décor, gifts, appliances); selects seasonal SKUs
Merch Planner determines store-level assortment by format (flagship/standard/compact); Buyer places seasonal POs with vendors; confirms delivery timeline 6–8 weeks before season start

fields.Participants: DC Ops Mgr, Merch Planner, Logistics Mgr

Automation Opportunity: - Allocation auto-generated from the assortment plan × store-cluster demand; outbound auto-scheduled against the store display-readiness flag
Controls: - CTL-21: seasonal inventory tracked separately to prevent commingling with sellable stock; operational: DC Ops Manager staging-plan sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **DC-congestion risk**: seasonal inventory arrives in bulk and competes for DC staging space with regular replenishment; mitigated by the pre-season staging reservation and cross-dock-fast-forward for high-volume seasonal SKUs

- **Mis-timed-outbound risk**: DC ships to stores before the display zone is ready, leaving seasonal inventory in the backroom; mitigated by the outbound shipment aligned with the W2384 display-setup readiness signal
System Touchpoints: - WMS (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving/putaway, W106 dispatch) — seasonal-inventory receiving, staging, and outbound
- Allocation (links to VS-02 / W4 replenishment, W105 multi-channel allocation) — the SKU-per-store-group allocation
- Inventory (links to VS-05 / W220 slow-moving tracking) — seasonal inventory flagged as time-bound
Time Estimate: ~1.5 weeks/season × 6 seasons across 4 DCs = **~350–500 hours/year** DC Ops + Merch Planner.

steps.activity: Merch Planner provides DC with seasonal allocation plan: quantity per SKU per store group; DC receives seasonal inventory; stages for store allocation; schedules outbound shipments aligned with store display readiness

fields.Participants: Merch Coord, Store Managers, Regional Ops

Automation Opportunity: - Display-plan auto-distributed per format; compliance-photo auto-scored against the spec (links to VS-55 W2175 pattern)
Controls: - CTL-421 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Planning & Phase-In Management (PA-64.1).)
- operational: planogram currency; operational: Merchandising Planner compliance-photo sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Compliance-variance risk**: stores interpret the display plan differently, producing inconsistent execution across the chain; mitigated by the detailed visual-merchandising guide and the compliance-photo verification

- **Window-pressure risk**: the 1-week window collides with regular store ops, producing rushed execution; mitigated by the W2389 transition planning that sequences the outgoing-season teardown with the incoming-season setup
System Touchpoints: - Planogram (links to VS-55 / W2166 seasonal refresh, W314 planogram template) — the seasonal display spec
- Store comms (links to VS-07 / W571) — the display-plan distribution and compliance-photo return
- VS-55 / W2181 planogram-change-implementation tracking — the compliance-verification pattern
Time Estimate: ~1 week/season Coordinator + ~4 hours/store setup × 200 stores × 6 seasons = **~5,000–6,000 hours/year** Coordinator + Store teams (setup absorbed into store-ops).

steps.activity: Coordinator distributes seasonal display plan: zone assignment, product list, signage, visual merchandising guide; stores set up within 1-week window; compliance photos submitted and verified

Automation Opportunity: - Markdown-trigger auto-armed at the configured sell-through threshold (links to W2390); seasonal-price auto-pushed to POS/label
Controls: - CTL-421 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Planning & Phase-In Management (PA-64.1).)
- CTL-421 (price/promo accuracy — links to VS-08 / W69 price-compliance audit); operational: Category Manager sign-off on the seasonal pricing plan
Pain Points / Risks: - **DTI-promo-permit risk**: a seasonal promo requires the "Per DTI Permit No." (links to W833 campaign compliance review); missing it triggers a DTI complaint (W2682); mitigated by the promo-setup checklist that gates activation on the DTI-permit field

- **Margin-erosion risk**: aggressive launch promos + planned markdowns compress seasonal margin below plan; mitigated by the W2397 post-clearance reconciliation feeding the next season's pricing model
System Touchpoints: - Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-57 / W107 pricing-hierarchy governance) — the seasonal price and markdown-trigger configuration
- Promo setup (links to VS-14 / W13 promotions, W262 store promotional setup, VS-58 coupon) — the seasonal promo
- Price-tag (links to VS-08 / W181) — the label generation for the seasonal price

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst sets seasonal pricing: launch price (may include early-bird promo), regular price, planned markdown triggers (based on sell-through rate); configures in ERP per VS-57

fields.Participants: HR Training Mgr, Category Mgr, Store Managers

Automation Opportunity: - Training auto-assigned per role 2 weeks pre-launch; completion-rate auto-reported to Store Managers
Controls: - CTL-421 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Planning & Phase-In Management (PA-64.1).)
- Operational: HR Training Manager completion-rate sign-off per store
Pain Points / Risks: - **Just-in-time-failure risk**: the training lands too close to the season launch and staff aren't ready when customers ask; mitigated by the 2-week-pre-launch training trigger
- **Completion-gap risk**: store staff don't complete the e-learning module and the knowledge gap shows up as missed sales; mitigated by the LMS completion-tracking with Store Manager follow-up
System Touchpoints: - LMS (links to VS-19.4 / W51 training calendar & compliance tracking) — the e-learning platform and completion tracking
- Product knowledge (links to VS-124 / sales enablement, VS-137 PIM) — the seasonal product content
- Store comms (links to VS-07 / W571) — the store-meeting-guide distribution
Time Estimate: ~1 week/season HR Training + ~30 min/staff module × ~5,800 staff = **~3,000–3,500 hours/year** HR + Store staff (staff time absorbed into store-ops).

steps.activity: Category Manager provides product knowledge materials: new seasonal products, features, selling points, FAQs; HR Training distributes via e-learning platform and store meeting guides

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, Category Mgr, Analytics Manager

Automation Opportunity: - Sell-through-vs-plan auto-flagged daily; slow-starter/fast-seller auto-categorized with suggested action
Controls: - CTL-421 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Planning & Phase-In Management (PA-64.1).)
- Operational: Category Manager daily-flash review sign-off during the launch window
Pain Points / Risks: - **False-alarm risk**: a slow first 3 days triggers a premature markdown on a SKU that was just waiting for the weekend traffic; mitigated by the 2-week observation window before action and the weekday-vs-weekend normalization

- **Reorder-too-late risk**: a fast seller is identified but the import reorder lead time (10–12 weeks) means it won't arrive in-season; mitigated by the W2388 vendor coordination for expedite/transfer options
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, W208 retail analytics) — the daily sell-through dashboard
- Replenishment (links to VS-02 / W4, W56 backorder) — the fast-seller reorder trigger
- Markdown (links to VS-64 / W2390) — the slow-starter markdown trigger
Time Estimate: ~30 min/day × ~10 launch days/season × 6 seasons = **~30 hours/year** Planner + system automated.

steps.activity: System monitors daily sell-through: compares vs. plan; identifies slow starters (may need markdown acceleration) and fast sellers (may need reorder); daily flash report to Category Manager

Automation Opportunity: - Seasonal-vendor term sheet auto-assembled from the agreement master; delivery-status auto-tracked against the season-start date
Controls: - CTL-39: rebate/markdown-allowance accuracy; CTL-48 (rebate-dispute resolution); operational: Category Manager sign-off on seasonal vendor terms
Pain Points / Risks: - **Markdown-support-dispute risk**: the vendor agreed to markdown support but disputes the unsold-quantity claim at season end; mitigated by the documented return/swap agreement term and the W2394 allowance calculation

- **Delivery-slippage risk**: a seasonal vendor delivers late, missing the season window entirely; mitigated by the 6–8 week pre-season delivery target and the vendor-scorecard penalty for late seasonal delivery
System Touchpoints: - Vendor agreement (links to VS-03 / W36 vendor onboarding, VS-39 / W27 rebate & co-op, VS-100 / W230 contracts) — the seasonal terms
- Vendor scorecard (links to VS-67 / W2458) — the vendor's seasonal-performance record
- Markdown allowance (links to VS-64 / W2394) — the markdown-support term
Time Estimate: ~1.5 weeks/season × 6 seasons across ~75 vendors = **~250–350 hours/year** Buyer.

steps.activity: Buyer confirms with vendors: delivery dates, quantities, quality standards, marketing support (co-op funds), markdown support (return/swap agreements for unsold seasonal inventory)

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, Category Mgr, DC Ops, Store Ops

Automation Opportunity: - Transition-window timeline auto-generated per zone; outgoing-remainder auto-flagged for consolidation
Controls: - CTL-421 (ensure controlled execution — Seasonal Planning & Phase-In Management (PA-64.1).)
- operational: planogram transition currency; operational: Merchandising Planner transition-completion sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Zone-handover-collision risk**: the outgoing season's clearance event and the incoming season's setup collide in the same zone and the same week, confusing customers and overwhelming staff; mitigated by the sequenced handover (clearance completes, then teardown, then setup) within the transition window

- **Outgoing-season-remainder risk**: the outgoing season's inventory isn't fully cleared before the incoming setup, forcing it into the backroom (dead stock); mitigated by the W2393 clearance-inventory consolidation before the handover
System Touchpoints: - Seasonal calendar (links to VS-29 / W306) — the season-overlap window
- Planogram transition (links to VS-55 / W2166, W264 seasonal transition) — the zone handover
- Replenishment (links to VS-02 / W4) — the outgoing→incoming replenishment switch
Time Estimate: ~1.5 weeks/transition × 6 transitions + DC/Store coordination absorbed = **~300–400 hours/year** Planner + coordination.

steps.activity: Planner manages transition: outgoing seasonal markdown (clear remaining), incoming seasonal setup (stage new display); coordinates display zone handover; adjusts replenishment from outgoing to incoming
